# Results — Study 324 (Bitcoin-Treasury) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). MicroStrategy (**MSTR**)
decomposed onto **BTC-USD** with simple daily returns: the slope is its **beta to
Bitcoin** (the leverage), the intercept its residual **alpha**, the HAC (Newey-West)
t-stat on the intercept the inference-bar number. Then the honest race — hold MSTR vs a
synthetic **levered-BTC replica** at MSTR's own beta, net of borrow, on excess-of-cash
Sharpe — and a NAV-premium-timing overlay. As-of **2026-06-17**; match the fingerprint to
confirm you hold the same tape.*

## Data stamp

| Series | Window (common days) | Days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| MSTR & BTC-USD — **full** | 2014-09-17 → 2026-06-17 | 2,955 | — |
| MSTR & BTC-USD — **treasury era** (≥ 2020-08-11) | 2020-08-11 → 2026-06-17 | 1,470 | `2f6382918332` |

> **The era matters.** MicroStrategy only *became* a "Bitcoin treasury" on **2020-08-11**,
> when Michael Saylor announced the company's first BTC purchase. Before that it was a
> no-growth enterprise-software stock with essentially no Bitcoin sensitivity (full-sample
> beta to BTC is just **0.45**, R² **18%**). Every headline below is the **treasury era**;
> mixing in 2014–2020 corrupts the very thing we're measuring. Total-return (auto-adjusted)
> closes both legs; inner-joined on the days both quote.

## How much of MSTR is just Bitcoin? — the decomposition

| Era | beta to BTC | R² | alpha (bps/day) | alpha (%/yr) | HAC *t*(alpha) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Treasury (2020-08 →) | **1.13** | **50.0%** | +10.8 | +39.3% | **+1.08** |
| Full (2014-09 →) | 0.45 | 18.0% | +5.4 | +19.6% | +0.76 |

- In the treasury era MSTR moves like **~1.1× Bitcoin**, and **half its daily variance is
  literally just BTC moving**. The residual alpha looks large (+39%/yr) but its
  **HAC *t* = +1.08 is well below the inference bar** (|t| ≥ 2). On this tape we *cannot*
  certify that MSTR is anything more than levered Bitcoin plus noise.
- The leverage is also **unstable**: 90-day rolling beta swings from **0.55 to 1.73**
  (median 1.20). "1.1× Bitcoin" is an average, not a contract.

## Does holding MSTR beat holding BTC? — the honest race

Hold MSTR vs a synthetic **levered-BTC replica** that takes the same 1.13× exposure and
pays borrow (8%/yr on the borrowed 0.13 notional). Excess-of-cash Sharpe (cash 3%/yr):

| | CAGR | Sharpe (excess) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **MSTR** | **+70.9%** | +1.01 | **−89.3%** |
| BTC (1×) | +53.7% | +0.92 | −76.6% |
| Levered-BTC replica (1.13×, net borrow) | +55.1% | +0.91 | −81.3% |

- MSTR's higher CAGR vs BTC is **leverage, not skill** — that's what a >1 beta does.
- Against its own levered replica MSTR adds **+11.0 bps/day**, but **HAC *t* = +1.10** and
  the **block-bootstrap 95% CI is [−8.6, +31.2] bps/day — it straddles zero.** The
  "treasury premium" did not pay a statistically distinguishable edge over plain leverage.
- MSTR took a **worse drawdown than even the levered replica** (−89% vs −81%): you bore the
  premium's extra risk without a reliable extra return.

## Does the NAV premium pay? — premium timing

MSTR's price swings far above and below the value of the coins it holds (our price-proxy
premium ranges **−0.99 to +1.02 log units**, std 0.38 — an enormous wobble). A contrarian
overlay — hold MSTR only when its premium is below its median, signal at close of *t* for
the *t+1* return (one execution lag), 5 bps one-way cost — versus always-hold:

| | CAGR | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|
| Always-hold MSTR | +70.9% | +1.03 |
| Premium-timed (cheap-only) | +67.7% | +1.06 |

The daily (timed − always) difference is **−9.3 bps/day, HAC *t* = −0.88** — *negative* and
insignificant. The premium mean-reverts, but timing it earned **nothing**: it is
return-free variance (risk you carry, not a coupon you collect), and a naive cheap/dear
rule sits out exactly the days the leverage compounds.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** In the only era that matters (post-2020-08 treasury era), MSTR is
  **~1.1× Bitcoin with 50% of its variance explained by BTC**, and the residual alpha
  (HAC *t* = +1.08) **does not clear the inference bar**. Literature and headlines say
  "MSTR is a leveraged Bitcoin bet" — and on this tape it is *only* that; the extra return
  is not statistically distinguishable from the leverage.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** MSTR's outperformance over BTC is leverage you could replicate
  with a levered-BTC position more cheaply and with a **smaller drawdown**; the wrapper's
  edge over its own replica has a CI that spans zero, and the NAV premium can't be timed.
  You pay a fluctuating premium for risk you can rent elsewhere.
- **Just leveraged Bitcoin? — CONFIRMED.** Beta ≈ 1.1, R² = 50%, no robust residual alpha,
  no harvestable premium. The "Bitcoin treasury" story is, on the tape, a leverage story.

*Not investment advice — research & education.*
